alternatives.differences: Magneto-inductive technology, nanotesla resolution, no hysteresis; different package, interface, and register map; higher precision but different footprint and supply requirements; needs new PCB and firmware.

results.summary: The Honeywell HMC5883L has been discontinued with end-of-life orders due by March 31, 2016 and final shipments by September 30, 2016, making it obsolete.
results.recommendation: Choose QMC5883L for fastest migration — it shares the HMC5883L footprint and I2C interface, so only a library change is needed, and it is widely available at low cost.

alternatives.differences: Marketed as pin-to-pin alternative. Same 32Mbit, 2.7-3.6V, SPI/Dual/Quad, SOIC-8, -40 to 85°C. Different manufacturer → different device ID (RDID), dummy clock cycles, and possibly status register layout. Firmware must handle new ID and any timing deltas.
alternatives.source_title: The Ultimate Guide: GigaDevice GD25Q as a Pin-to-Pin Alternative to Winbond W25Q Series - Ovaga Technologies

alternatives.differences: Cross-vendor 32Mbit SPI NOR flash in same SOIC-8 package. Wider temp range (-40 to 105°C). Page program time 4ms vs 3ms. Different device ID, register map, and command set. Firmware updates required for ID, write/erase timing, and protection bits.

results.summary: The Winbond W25Q32JVSSIQ is obsolete per manufacturer notice but currently in stock from distributors and is RoHS compliant.
results.recommendation: Start with Winbond W25Q32RV — it is the manufacturer's direct successor, minimizing register and timing surprises; validate RDID and erase/program times before cutover.
